strokeOrderNote: Two movements in one continuous pen-down run; 479 of 479 POH-Db samples (100%) are one stroke.

strokeOrderSource.citation: POH-Db, Persian Online Handwriting Database (SLT Lab, Amirkabir University of Technology; github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db at commit 018b039, Writepads/NumberGroup; AGPL-3.0, facts only): 479 aligned samples of ۸ from 29 native writers; one stroke in 479 (100%); starts at the bottom left in 373 (78%)
strokeOrderSource.variation: Counted for this record from POH-Db's NumberGroup writepads: lines of Persian numbers that native writers wrote on FarsiHandwriting.ir with a pen, a finger or a stylus (112 writepads by 30 writers; the mouse writepads were left out), recorded as InkML, where each trace is one pen-down stroke. Each line was split into characters by horizontal overlap; of the 1,046 lines whose character count matched their label, the 1,005 whose characters ran left to right were used (which also shows that the numbers are written left to right). Zones are thirds of each character's box, and the split is heuristic, so the shares are approximate. Of 479 samples of ۸, 479 (100%) are one stroke. 373 (78%) start at the bottom left and 324 (68%) first move up; the highest point comes in the middle of the stroke in 463 (97%), and 453 (95%) end at the bottom right: up to the peak, then down. POH-Db is licensed AGPL-3.0, so only these counts and shares are taken; no coordinate or trace is copied, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Naskh Arabic outline rather than to any sample. Handwriting varies by writer.
